about: Hand-picked finds, rotated a few at a time on the home page and listed in full at /highlights. Dated ones disappear after `until`. `tag` is the small label; `line` says why it's worth the time. Curated 2026-10-28.

items.line: Root Division's Studio Artist programme: a subsidised studio in exchange for teaching. Applications close November 1.
The Textile Arts Council's bazaar at St Mary's: world and vintage textiles, and a room full of Bay Area weavers to meet.
Oakland studio with classes, a residency and outside firing. MerrittFest on November 7 is an easy way in.
A whole museum of lace and textiles in Berkeley, free to visit, with small classes attached (beaded cabochons on November 14).
Letterpress and bookbinding in the Mission. The spring workshop schedule goes up November 14; the Betsy Davids show runs to December 20.
The Crucible's holiday craft fair in Oakland: glass, metal, wood and clay, made by the people who teach there.
A free artist fair in the Mission, a good afternoon to see who's making what in the city.
US$3,000 a month for four to six weeks with one of the great decorative-arts collections. The portal opens November 1; drafts reviewed until December 1.
Free to enter, judged from photos, open to everyone. The Grand Prix is five million yen.
A cone 10 studio for experienced potters in San Anselmo. Their 2027 residency is free; applications close January 30.
Rose B. Simpson's figures fill Wilsey Court at the de Young: clay at its most monumental, included with admission.
SFMOMA's survey of Northern California craft, 1945 to 1980: where the Bay's studio-pottery world came from.
An open invitation to teach here. Their SoMa studio is on 9th Street; résumés go to jobs@clayroomsf.com.
Cone 10, 24-hour member access, high ceilings, on Folsom at 20th. Visiting hours Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday afternoons.
Naturally dyed yarn and fabric, mending and dye supplies, and classes, in Oakland. Open to shop on Fridays and Saturdays.
Jess Taylor makes glazes from local granite above Inverness and publishes every test: the closest thing in the Bay to a wild-materials glaze practice.
Clay, raw glaze materials and plaster in the city, with free parking out back. Weekdays 9 to 3; the bigger Richmond store opens Saturdays.
A six-week Glaze Design and Mixing course in the Mission, plus their own handmade glazes to buy while building up a shelf.
SF State's ceramics programme has a real glaze room and teaches glaze calculation; they also keep a standing pool of lecturers.
Watch Heath's tile being made in the Mission (tours need an RSVP), then the showroom and Tartine next door.
Fibershed's learning centre in Point Reyes: fibre grown, dyed and woven within a day's drive, taught in small workshops.
The Museum of the African Diaspora, by Yerba Buena. Its emerging-artist programme and residencies are worth knowing about.
Berkeley's weaving guild meets on the third Monday of the month. The realistic way into loom time, and into the weaving community, in the East Bay.
Up to US$100,000 for cultural projects, applied for through a Rwandan NGO or cooperative: the route for scaling up a project in Rwanda. Usually opens in March.
